statement: The first line holds n. Print every binary string of length n that has no two 1s side by side, in increasing lexicographic order, separated by single spaces on one line. Build them recursively: at each position try 0 and then 1, and allow a 1 only when the previously placed character was 0 or the string is still empty. Trying 0 before 1 makes the output lexicographic automatically.
constraints: Output strings are separated by single spaces.

example.why: Five strings of length 3 avoid adjacent 1s; 011, 110 and 111 all fail.

hint: Carry one boolean down the recursion - whether the last placed character was a 1.
mistake: Building all strings and scanning each for 11 at the leaf, instead of pruning while placing.
